title: Concrete Simulator Query Complexity for Iterated Blockciphers
summary: Classical analysis gives only a polynomial simulator-query bound for iterated blockciphers with at most three primitive calls; a fully concrete characterization remains open.

formal_statement.body: For indifferentiability of iterated blockciphers constructed from at most three primitive calls, determine a fully concrete characterization of the simulator's query complexity. Existing classical treatment bounds this complexity only polynomially, and that bound appears incompatible with concrete analyses; resolving the gap may require a new paradigm.

scope.domain: Indifferentiability analysis of iterated blockciphers built from at most three primitive calls.
parameters: Primitive-call count: limits the iterated-blockcipher construction to at most three calls
Simulator query complexity: the resource to be characterized concretely
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine a fully concrete characterization of the simulator's query complexity despite the apparent mismatch between the classical polynomial bound and concrete analyses.

citations.label: Impossibility of Indifferentiable Iterated Blockciphers from 3 or Less Primitive Calls

progress.summary: The source states that classical treatment gives only a polynomial bound on simulator query complexity, which appears incompatible with concrete analyses. It leaves fully concrete characterizations for future work and suggests that a new paradigm may be needed.
citation_labels: Chun Guo et al., Impossibility of Indifferentiable Iterated Blockciphers from 3 or Less Primitive Calls
